A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same readable 11-page AdaCM2 paper, including matching equations, figures, tables and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix. The only visible difference is the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original AdaCM2 experiments on classification, captioning and question answering, including memory measurements and ablations in Tables 1–4 and Figures 6–8.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the same original experimental results, memory measurements and ablations reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain identical Q-Former processing, cross-modality token scoring, adaptive cache reduction and text-generation objectives.

E1.justification: Coverage remains LVU, Breakfast and COIN classification; MSRVTT-QA and MSVD-QA; and MSRVTT, MSVD and YouCook2 captioning. Figure 2 retains the same Ego4D case studies.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–4 and Figures 6–7, including MA-LMM comparisons, the random-eviction control and the FlanT5-XL/Vicuna-7B decoder comparison.

E3.justification: The reported metrics, model configurations, training procedure and 10 fps frame extraction in Sections 5.1–5.2 are unchanged. The ablation settings also match.

E4.justification: The attention analyses, Ego4D examples, memory analysis and ablations of eviction strategy, split/conserve ratios and decoder choice are identical.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Statistical and uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 retains average LVU accuracy of 67.5 for AdaCM2 and 63.0 for MA-LMM in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), their mathematical definitions and the cache-size convergence derivation in Section 4.2 are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain identical novelty, applicability, accuracy and memory-efficiency claims, including the claimed 4.5% LVU improvement and up-to-65% memory reduction.

C2.justification: Explanations connecting attention sparsity to memory reduction, redundant tokens to accuracy loss and LLM size to memory consumption are unchanged. Applicability and future-work statements also match.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 retains the same backbone versions, frozen/trainable components, preprocessing and hardware details. The reported alpha and beta settings remain 0.1, and no code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and all 55 numbered references are identical.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 19 Nov 2024 to v2 dated 18 Mar 2025. Manuscript prose, terminology and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Tables 1–4 and Algorithm 1 retain identical presentation, captions and placement. Page layout is unchanged; pages 2–11 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 changes only the administrative arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations and presentation remain identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
